title: openwiz.attachment.v1
description: OpenWiz 0.0.4 attachments: one ready attachment's verified record (the root), its kind, its readiness and the fixed list of failure reasons (B1 phase 1, the core's model); and the reports of openwiz attachment add, ls and rm (B1 phase 2: add_report, list_report, remove_report, each with its schema id). Ready means only that the controller holds a verified copy: nothing here is sent or uploaded. CloudRoom's limits behind the reasons (10 MiB per image, 25 MiB per file, the image limit for a file whose extension CloudRoom types as an image) are source-read, not observed.

attachment.description: One ready attachment: the whole copy is on the controller, with its size, SHA-256, kind and safe name verified. It claims nothing about CloudRoom.

display_name.description: The owner's original file name, unchanged: untrusted text, for display only. Never a path to open.

attachment_id.description: Chosen by the controller; opaque. 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, _ and -, starting with a letter or digit, so it is also one safe path segment.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the attachment's bytes.

kind.description: Decided from the bytes: image for PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP; file for everything else. Never from a declared MIME type.

safe_name.description: The staged name: the original's basename reduced to ASCII letters, digits,., _ and -, never starting with. or -. At most 179 bytes, so CloudRoom's stored name (this stem, '-<time>-<random>', this extension: up to 21 more bytes) fits the Cloud core's 200. The agent sees that stored name, not this one (source-read, not observed).

readiness.description: One attachment's readiness. selected and uploading exist only in clients and in an upload in flight; only ready claims a verified copy on the controller.

fail_reason.description: Why an attachment can't become ready: unsupported_heif (HEIC/HEIF, never converted), type_unclear (an ISO media file whose first bytes don't settle whether it is HEIF), extension_mismatch (the name and the bytes disagree), image_too_large (over 10 MiB), file_too_large (over 25 MiB), image_typed_file_too_large (a file CloudRoom types as an image by its extension, over 10 MiB), folder, low_disk (under the 1 GiB floor), size_mismatch, connection_lost, signed_out, unreadable.

staged.description: One attachment in the store, as a report shows it.

ready_at.description: When it became ready: Unix milliseconds.

expires_at.description: When it expires, 24 hours after it became ready; null while its operation may still use it.

add_report.description: openwiz attachment add --json: every path given, each in exactly one of ready, failed and not_staged, by its index; and what this run's open found past its time-to-live, and deleted.

items.description: A path whose verified copy is ready.

index.description: The path's or id's place in the command's arguments, from 0.

path.description: The path as given (any byte that isn't UTF-8 shown as U+FFFD): untrusted text.

items.description: A path that can't become ready: nothing of it was kept.

index.description: The path's or id's place in the command's arguments, from 0.

path.description: The path as given (any byte that isn't UTF-8 shown as U+FFFD): untrusted text.

items.description: A path the store failed on: nothing of it was kept. The error names no file.

index.description: The path's or id's place in the command's arguments, from 0.

path.description: The path as given (any byte that isn't UTF-8 shown as U+FFFD): untrusted text.

list_report.description: openwiz attachment ls --json: the ready attachments, oldest first; those whose metadata can't be read or whose copy isn't the size recorded; and what this run's open found past its time-to-live, and deleted.

items.description: Not ready: attachment rm deletes it.

remove_report.description: openwiz attachment rm --json: every id given, in order, with what was done; and what this run's open found past its time-to-live, and deleted.

index.description: The path's or id's place in the command's arguments, from 0.

result.description: removed: its copy and metadata are deleted; expired: this run's open deleted it at its time-to-live; refused: its operation is dispatching or uncertain, so it is kept; not_found: no staged attachment has this id; not_removed: the store failed on it.
